| Scene description | • S10-A is near Simenkou & Yellow Crane Tower Metro Station. Green and black wheeled bins line concrete beside green barriers; two black bins are annotated as overflowing and others as non-overflowing. Blue plastic drums and white paint buckets nearby contain residues or coverings; two blue drums are annotated as overflowing and two as accumulation. Striped and white canvas and blue dust sheeting suggest construction or temporary material storage. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should remain closed and clean, without spillage or scattered waste, and be collected regularly. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15.<br>• Construction or storage areas require dedicated collection facilities, separate storage, and no mixing or open stockpiling against pollution. Standard for Environment and Sanitation at Construction SitesJGJ 147-2016 Section 5.2.3.<br>• Overflow or accumulation retained beyond 24 hours constitutes management neglect requiring rectification. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 22.<br>• Verified improper public storage or dumping without timely removal may entail correction orders and fines. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 34.<br>• Collection points require clear labels, separate collection, and stronger inspections in busy station areas against cross-contamination. Signs for classification of municipal solid wasteGB/T 19095-2019 Section 6.2. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Four overflowing bins and two accumulated containers in busy station surroundings include construction-material drums, indicating sanitation risks and management gaps without extensive litter or obvious pollution. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: overflowing bins may scatter or leak waste, impairing appearance; residues in accumulated drums may cause insects or odors. Possible short-term impacts: cloudy, breezy weather may spread odors affecting passengers; rain may carry waste onto ground or into drains, causing secondary pollution. |
| Potential causes | - Construction storage may generate more waste than collection handles; blue drums, paint buckets, and dust sheeting indicate work activity.<br>- Insufficient capacity or delayed collection may affect black bins near station entrances during pedestrian peaks.<br>- Mixed, unlabeled drums suggest absent sorting management or dedicated temporary facilities.<br>- Review collection records, contractor waste plans, and service–generation matching. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, retained waste may breed insects and rodents and cause health problems; station-area complaints may damage urban appearance; and uncorrected problems may incur assessment deductions or penalties. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** empty overflowing and accumulated containers, separately remove drums and paint buckets, clear litter, and wash and disinfect bins against residual odors.<br>- **Long-term measures:** require contractors or managers to provide adequate temporary sorting capacity and at least daily collection; inspect and increase station-area collections; train construction staff and clarify responsibilities. |
| Priority | **High.** Sanitation and appearance risks in busy station surroundings, including temporary construction storage, may cause odors, vectors, or complaints. Priority action is needed to protect public environmental quality. |
